transcript_id.description: Echo the transcript id given in the prompt, exactly.

venue_type.description: Format of the appearance, inferred from the transcript itself.

venue_challenge.description: 1-5. 1 = promotional, no pushback. 3 = substantive interview with real follow-ups. 5 = adversarial or expert questioning that changes premises. Recorded for context; it does not alter the scores.

venue_challenge_reason.description: One or two sentences citing what in the transcript sets this level.

subject_speech_share_pct.description: 0-100. Your estimate of the share of words in this transcript spoken by the SUBJECT rather than an interviewer, host, or other participant.

attribution_confidence.description: How confident you are that you correctly separated the subject's speech from everyone else's. Captions carry no speaker labels.

attribution_notes.description: How you told the turns apart, and where you were unsure.

identity_guess.description: If the transcript is blinded, who or what kind of speaker do you think this is? Write 'unknown' if you genuinely cannot tell. This measures how well the blinding held; it must not influence any score.

identity_confident.description: True only if you are confident you know the specific individual.

identity_basis.description: What gave the identity away, or why it stayed hidden.

asr_quality.description: How badly automatic speech recognition damaged this transcript. Heavy corruption should lower your stated confidence, not the scores.

asr_notes.description: Specific corrupted terms you had to read through, and any passage you could not interpret.

subcriteria.description: All 15 sub-criteria, in order: C1 C2 C3 C4 I1 I2 I3 I4 I5 I6 I7 T1 T2 T3 T4.

code.description: One of C1 C2 C3 C4 I1 I2 I3 I4 I5 I6 I7 T1 T2 T3 T4

score.description: 1 to 5, or 0 meaning NOT OBSERVED because the conversation gave no reasonable opportunity to demonstrate it. Use 0 rather than a middling score to fill a gap.

justification.description: One or two sentences. If the score is 0, say why the format gave no opportunity.

overall.description: 0.20*d1 + 0.45*d2 + 0.35*d3, computed from your own dimension scores.

coverage.description: Share of the 15 sub-criteria you scored rather than marked not observed, as a decimal between 0 and 1.

confidence_reason.description: Why this confidence: transcript length, attribution difficulty, speech recognition damage, or coverage.

salient_claims.description: The two to four most substantive specific claims the SUBJECT made, each stated in your own words in one sentence. Not quotes. These let a reader see what the score is about.

red_flags.description: Anything that should worry a careful listener: a confident technical claim that is wrong on its face, quantities used incoherently, a question dodged and never returned to, a premise accepted uncritically. Empty array if none.

score.description: 1 to 100, anchored by the band descriptions in the rubric.

reasoning.description: Several sentences in your own words explaining what in the transcript produced this number. This is read by a human auditor who may disagree with you, so make the argument, do not just assert the score.

evidence.description: Two to four short quotations from the SUBJECT supporting the score.

quote.description: 25 words maximum, verbatim from the transcript. Quote only the fragment you need. Longer quotes will be rejected.

timestamp.description: Nearest [hh:mm:ss] marker in the transcript, or 'unmarked' if none is near.

why_it_matters.description: One sentence on what this fragment demonstrates.

counterevidence.description: The strongest thing in this transcript that argues against the score you gave. If there is genuinely none, say so and explain why.
